transcript.content: Hello. What brings you to the clinic today?

Once I start eating in the evenings, it feels like I can’t stop myself, no matter how much I tell myself I should. It's really starting to scare me because I've always been a very disciplined person who keeps things under control.
After these episodes of overeating, do you do anything to try to prevent weight gain, such as making yourself throw up, fasting, or exercising excessively?

It's hard to admit, but on those nights when I lose control, I end up going to the bathroom and forcing myself to throw up. I tell myself I'm just getting the bad stuff out so it doesn't turn into extra weight, and this has been happening about once a week.
How long has this cycle of overeating and forcing yourself to throw up been going on? Has it been happening for at least three months?

Yes, it's been going on for about five months now, which is definitely longer than three months. It happens at least once a week in the evening, and it all started right after my doctor raised concerns about my blood pressure and weight.
How much do your body weight and shape influence how you judge or feel about yourself as a person?

Honestly, it has a massive hold on me lately. I catch myself thinking that doing a good job at work or being a good husband doesn’t even matter if my gut is hanging over my belt. It's like my whole worth as a man comes down to how big I look in a dress shirt.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets all diagnostic criteria for Bulimia Nervosa (ICD-10: F50.2). He describes recurrent episodes of binge eating characterized by a feeling of loss of control, followed by inappropriate compensatory behavior (self-induced vomiting) to prevent weight gain. These episodes have occurred at least once a week for approximately five months (exceeding the three-month threshold). Additionally, his self-evaluation is unduly influenced by his body shape and weight.
